# Psalm 81 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** To the choirmaster: according to the Gittith. Of Asaph. Sing aloud to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob!

**2** Raise a song; sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre with the harp.

**3** Blow the trumpet at the new moon, at the full moon, on our feast day.

**4** For it is a statute for Israel, a rule of the God of Jacob.

**5** He made it a decree in Joseph when he went out over the land of Egypt. I hear a language I had not known:

**6** "I relieved your shoulder of the burden; your hands were freed from the basket.

**7** In distress you called, and I delivered you; I answered you in the secret place of thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah

**8** Hear, O my people, while I admonish you! O Israel, if you would but listen to me!

**9** There shall be no strange god among you; you shall not bow down to a foreign god.

**10** I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.

**11** "But my people did not listen to my voice; Israel would not submit to me.

**12** So I gave them over to their stubborn hearts, to follow their own counsels.

**13** Oh, that my people would listen to me, that Israel would walk in my ways!

**14** I would soon subdue their enemies and turn my hand against their foes.

**15** Those who hate the LORD would cringe toward him, and their fate would last forever.

**16** But he would feed you with the finest of the wheat, and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you."

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 81.

- **81:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **81:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **81:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **81:11** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **81:12** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **81:14** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **81:3**: Trumpet (shofar) at the new moon and full moon — likely refers to the Feast of Tabernacles (Sukkot), which begins at the full moon of Tishri.
- **81:10**: 'Open-wide your-mouth and-I-will-fill-it' — stunning image of God's generosity; Israel need only receive.

### LOGOS
- **81:5b-16**: God speaks directly in first person for most of the psalm — one of the longest divine speeches in the Psalter. It echoes the covenant formula of Sinai.
- **81:13-16**: The conditional 'if only' expresses divine longing — God's desire for obedience is portrayed as parental yearning, not authoritarian demand.

### PNEUMA
- **81:10**: This verse captures God's heart perfectly: 'I am the LORD your God... Open your mouth wide and I will fill it.' God isn't stingy — he's generous beyond imagination. We just need to receive.
- **81:13-14**: There's something deeply moving about God saying 'if only.' The Almighty Creator, longing for his people to just listen. It's not anger — it's heartbreak.

— SOPHIA
